---STATUS---
# pathland-render-qt — implementation status

**Last updated:** September 28, 2026

The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.

**Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
- **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
  **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
  the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
  and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
- **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
  QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
  delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
  needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative`).

## Implemented

- **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
  Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
  links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
  `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
  core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
- **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
  `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
  set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
  `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
- **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
  emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
  commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
  preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
  renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
  clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
  are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
  `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
- **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
  `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → a **wrapper `Item` holding an inner
  `ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`QtQuick.Layouts`; the wrapper's `plPad` drives
  padding + implicit size, so a stack hugs its content), `GRID`+lazy grids →
  `Grid`, `ZSTACK` → `Item`, `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView` (content attaches to its
  `contentItem`; fills its parent by default), `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
  unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR`/`SHAPE` → `Rectangle`,
  `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
  → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
  handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
  activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
  (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
  `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
  (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
  `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
  native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
  (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
  FILL → **`Layout.fillWidth`/`fillHeight` in a layout, anchors.fill elsewhere**,
  `-2` HUG → implicit), color, **font size/weight/family via the `font` `QFont`
  property** (dotted-path `setProperty` silently fails), opacity, visible, z,
  value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
  `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode`, progress/indeterminate, selection→currentIndex,
  prompt/label→placeholder, image source. **Stack alignment**: a stack's
  `ALIGNMENT` is applied to each child via its `Layout` attached properties
  (`Fill` stretches the cross axis; Start/Center/End set `Layout.alignment`).
  **Roots are anchored to fill the window** (GTK hexpand/vexpand parity).
  `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned style defaults (value props untouched so a
  slider/toggle doesn't lose position on echo).
- **Diff ordering** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer::diff` emits child inserts
  *before* property deltas, so `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` land after a widget is
  attached to its final parent — FILL resolves against the real parent instead of
  the create-time contentItem placeholder.
- **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
  (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
  `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
  ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
  `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
- **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
  is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
  its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
  Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
  spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
  `DELETE`.
- **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
  `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
  renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
- **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
  fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
  shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
  concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
  init.
- **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
  `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
  C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
- **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
  an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
  idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
- **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
  on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
  `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
  `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
  a bare program name to Qt.
- **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
  Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
  the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
  shared ring).

- **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
  `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
  page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
  `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
  depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
  chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
  `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
  pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
  is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
  has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
  QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
  container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
  visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Pointer `hover`/`leave` flags (`POINTER_MOVE` hovering/leaving) and
  `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` listener bits are not yet reported; BackSpace as native
  back (text-focus detection) is deferred.
- The Rust DSL does not yet expose signal property bindings (the Java DSL
  does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
  tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.
- The Rust DSL has no `NavigationContainer` either (the spec table is
  aspirational) — the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH, but the Rust demo
  can't exercise nav without a DSL feature; Java/SplitNavDemo is the nav demo
  vehicle (Phase D).
- `TRANSITION`-hint animation, back-swipe gestures, multi-step deep-link
  intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).
- `BACKGROUND_COLOR`/border on stacks/controls (Qt Quick Controls own their
  background delegate; mapping is a follow-up), `SHAPE` path approximation,
  `MENU` popup item list, `DATE_PICKER`/`COLOR_PICKER` native dialogs, and
  `PICKER` option styling not yet mapped.
- **FILL inside plain positioners**: `GRID` (a `QQuickGrid`) rejects
  `anchors.fill` on its children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a Grid
  defers and is skipped (the positioner sizes it). Stacks use `RowLayout`/
  `ColumnLayout` so FILL children stretch properly; `Row`/`Column`/`Grid`
  plain-positioner stretch would need `QtQuick.Layouts` everywhere.
- **Java JNA demo** (`lib/java/pathland-qt-demo`) runs the shared
  `SplitNavDemo` (incl. native navigation) via `pathland_qt_run_ring` — the
  cross-language nav demo vehicle, since the Rust DSL lacks a
  `NavigationContainer`.
- Lazy views render eagerly.

## Verified by

`cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (needs Qt6 dev libs; offscreen for the FFI
tests) — the delta diff suite, the end-to-end FFI batch
(`command_batch_crosses_into_cpp_offscreen`), the **full pipeline**
(`renderer_drives_live_qml_scene`: DSL → engine → frame → shared decode →
delta diff → FFI → live QML `Column`/`Text`/`Button`/`Slider` with spacing/value
applied and a delta re-applied), **FILL/Layout stretch**
(`fill_child_stretches_inside_stack`: FILL → `Layout.fillWidth`, fixed →
`Layout.preferredWidth`, stack `ALIGNMENT=FILL` stretches the cross axis, root
anchored to the window), pointer-listener MouseArea attachment
(`pointer_listeners_attach_mousearea`), the event path
(`decode_maps_pointer_and_global_events`, `ring_event_writes_pointer_into_ring_and_wakes`,
`scheme_event_reapplies_without_waking`, `text_event_string_is_length_prefixed`,
`frame_has_reset_detects_meta_reset`), and Phase-B control coverage
(`control_widgets_construct_and_apply_props`, `picker_builds_model_from_option_children`),
and the nav adapter (`nav_slot_promotes_and_pushes_root_page`,
`nav_depth_push_and_pop`, `nav_replace_same_depth_new_route`,
`nav_custom_chrome_bare_pages`). Full workspace: `cd lib/rust && cargo test`.
Java JNA demo: `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` (headless `RingEventReaderTest`
runs in the Maven reactor; the live host mounts `SplitNavDemo`).
Demo: `scripts/run-rust-qt-demo.sh`.

# Pathland Media Kit

**Wire protocol version:** 1
**Status:** Draft
**Last Updated:** October 17, 2026

---

## Introduction

Media playback in Pathland is split into two roles:

- a **media controller** ([`MEDIA_CONTROLLER`](./PRIMITIVES.md#media-controller--media_controller-0x30)
  `0x30`) — a **non-visual** node that owns a media resource and its transport
  state (source, play/pause, position, volume, …); and
- a **video surface** ([`VIDEO`](./PRIMITIVES.md#video--video-0x0a) `0x0A`) — the
  only media *view*: it references a controller and renders its video output.

**Audio has no view of its own.** Audio is non-visual: an audio playback is a
controller plus the application's **own** views (buttons, sliders, labels) bound
to the controller's transport signals. There are **no renderer-native audio
controls** — the application defines the entire control surface in code. The
former `AUDIO` component is therefore **removed**.

Before this document, playback identity *was* the media node id: the source and
the transport properties lived on the `AUDIO`/`VIDEO` node itself, and the media
events reported against it. That makes a **structural swap** of the media node —
the normal case under `SIZE_THAT_FITS`, conditional rendering, or any subtree
replacement — destroy the playback, and it makes "control the same playback from
two places" inexpressible.

The controller/surface split fixes both: playback identity is the **controller**
node id, which the application keeps **outside** the swapping branch, so a swap
re-attaches a view to a playback that never stopped — and for audio the swapping
thing is just the application's own control views.

There is **one** controller component for both audio and video — the transport is
the same thing in both cases, exactly as SwiftUI has one `AVPlayer` for both and
`VideoPlayer` is merely a view over it. **Kind is decided by the views**: a
controller with a `VIDEO` surface renders video; a controller with no media view
is audio.

This document specifies the media contract: the controller node, the video
surface binding, transport commands vs. reports, the event family, and the swap
rules. It adds **one component**, **five properties**, and **one event**, and
removes the `AUDIO` component — no new opcode category, and no change to the wire
format.

### Relationship to the other specs

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md) | Wire format (16-byte opcode, categories, value types, `PLPL` batches) |
| [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) | The `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` component and the `VIDEO` surface |
| [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md) | The media property ids and their value types |
| [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) | The `MEDIA_*` event family, its guards, and the echo rules |
| [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md) | The controller's layout transparency and media content fitting |
| [CONFORMANCE.md](./CONFORMANCE.md) | Golden vectors for the controller component and the binding property |
| **MEDIA.md** (this file) | The end-to-end media contract |

---

## 1. The model

```
MEDIA_CONTROLLER 0x30            non-visual; owns the resource + transport
  MEDIA_SOURCE
  PLAYBACK_STATE / MEDIA_POSITION / MEDIA_VOLUME
  MEDIA_MUTED / MEDIA_LOOP / MEDIA_RATE
        ▲                                        ▲
        │ MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID                    │ bound transport signals
        │                                        │
   VIDEO 0x0A                            application views
   (renders the video output)            (buttons/sliders/labels —
                                          the ENTIRE audio control surface)
```

- The **controller** is a node in the application's retained tree, but it is
  **layout-transparent** (§2.2): it occupies no space and renders no element.
- A **video surface** is an ordinary view node wherever the application wants it
  in the layout. It names a controller with `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` (0x103A). It is
  **not** a child of the controller — the relationship is a **reference**, not a
  parent/child edge. The two nodes may live anywhere in the tree, and their
  relative position carries no meaning.
- **Audio has no view.** An audio playback is controlled by ordinary application
  views whose actions/values write the controller's transport properties. Nothing
  in the protocol renders audio.
- The application **SHOULD** place a controller at a stable position that no
  structural swap removes — e.g. a sibling of (or ancestor of) the `SIZE_THAT_FITS`
  slot, or a child of the root. A controller inside a swapping branch would be
  created and destroyed with that branch, defeating the split.

### 1.1 What lives where

| Concern | Owner |
|---------|-------|
| The media resource (source URL/asset) | controller — `MEDIA_SOURCE` |
| Transport state (play, seek, volume, mute, loop, rate) | controller |
| Transport **commands** from the app | controller (properties) |
| Transport **reports** to the app | controller (events target its id) |
| Whether a visual is shown, and its box/content mode | `VIDEO` surface |
| The video control UI (transport buttons, seek bar, volume) | `VIDEO` surface |
| The **audio** control UI (transport buttons, seek bar, volume) | the application's own views (no protocol surface) |
| Renderer-native vs. custom **video** controls | `VIDEO` dual mode (native when it has no children, the children when it has) |

---

## 2. The controller — `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30

### 2.1 Protocol

- A **leaf** node: it has no children. A `VIDEO` surface references it by id;
  it is not that surface's child.
- It carries the media resource and the transport properties (§2.3).
- It is created, updated, and deleted like any other node (`TREE` `CREATE_NODE` /
  `DELETE_NODE`), so it participates in the ordinary structural diff, in a
  full-snapshot (`META::RESYNC`), and in proxy-id remapping
  ([PROXY.md](./PROXY.md)) with no media-specific machinery.
- A controller is **not** a media surface and never renders a visual.

# Pathland Proxy Views

**Wire protocol version:** 1
**Status:** Draft
**Last Updated:** October 15, 2026

---

## Introduction

A **proxy view** ([`PROXY_VIEW`](./PRIMITIVES.md#proxyview--proxy_view-0x1e) `0x1E`)
lets one Pathland application compose views served by **several** Pathland
servers into a **single unified document**. The application that owns the proxy
node (the **proxying server**, "A") connects to another Pathland server (the
**origin server**, "B") as a Pathland **host** (client), receives B's subtree,
and splices it into its own opcode stream. The end client (a browser or a native
renderer) still talks to **one** server over **one** connection and applies
**one** opcode stream.

This document specifies the proxy contract: node-id namespacing, the snapshot
handshake, SSR embedding, event routing, lifecycle, and flow control. It uses
**only existing protocol surface** — there is no proxy-specific opcode.

> **Scope.** Nested proxies (B itself proxying C) are **not** part of this
> version; the id-range model below generalizes to them, but recursion, depth
> limits, and cycle detection beyond the direct case are deferred.

### Relationship to the other specs

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md) | Wire format (categories, commands, 16-byte opcode, PLPL batches, `META::RESYNC`) |
| [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md) | The `PROXY_VIEW` component and its layout semantics |
| [DSL.md](./DSL.md) | The `RemoteView` authoring surface |
| [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md) | Raw-input events routed across a proxy boundary |
| **PROXY.md** (this file) | The end-to-end proxy contract |

---

## 1. Roles

A proxying server occupies **two protocol roles at once**:

| Peer | A's role | Direction of A's traffic |
|------|----------|--------------------------|
| End client (browser / native renderer) | **guest** (app) | emits `TREE`/`PARAMETER` to the client; receives `EVENT` from the client |
| Origin server (B) | **host** (renderer) | receives `TREE`/`PARAMETER` from B; sends `EVENT` to B; sends `META::RESYNC` to B |

The protocol directions line up without modification: `TREE`/`PARAMETER` are
guest → host, `EVENT` is host → guest, and `META::RESYNC` is host → guest.

The origin server needs **no proxy awareness**: it serves a normal session (SSR
+ `/ws`) and cannot tell a proxying server from an ordinary client.

---

## 2. Node-id namespacing (MUST)

Node ids are per-emitter `u32` values; two independent emitters both start at
`1` and **collide**. A renderer that receives `CREATE_NODE` for an existing id
**merges** onto the existing node. A proxying server therefore MUST remap every
id in B's stream into a **disjoint high range** before emitting it to the client.

### 2.1 Reserved proxy id range

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| Range | `[0x4000_0000, 0x8000_0000)` |
| Block size | `0x0010_0000` (`2^20`, 1,048,576 ids) |
| Blocks | 1024 (one per proxy instance) |

A proxying server MUST NOT allocate its own node ids at or above `0x4000_0000`
(a conforming emitter asserts this).

### 2.2 Remap rule

For proxy instance `k` (0-based) and an origin node id `bId`:

```
base(k) = 0x4000_0000 + k * 0x0010_0000

# Icons — the `ICON` primitive and canonical vocabulary

The `ICON` primitive (0x0B) renders a **renderer-native symbol** for a canonical,
semantic name written once in the UI model. Unlike `IMAGE` (an asset loaded from
a URL), an icon is a *word* the renderer maps onto its platform's native icon
set.

> **The spec is the vocabulary contract only.** It lists the icons that are
> spec'ed — the `ICON_NAME` values every renderer MUST understand. **Which
> native glyph each renderer draws for a name is renderer-owned** (like the
> concrete values of design tokens): the mapping never appears in the spec;
> each renderer defines its own.

The **application owns the intent** (the neutral name); the **renderer owns the
visual** (which glyph, its default size, its weighting). This mirrors the design
tokens' split (spec/TOKENS.md).

## Protocol

- **Component**: `ICON` `0x0B` (leaf).
- **Property**: `ICON_NAME` `0x1038` (`STRING`, arena ref) — the canonical name.
- Reuses: `LABEL` (accessibility — a `LABEL` makes the icon presentable, absent
  makes it decorative), `COLOR` / `foregroundStyle` (tint), `FONT_SIZE` (size —
  text-style symbol sizing; the renderer owns its default size when absent), and
  the frame/opacity modifiers.
- `ICON` is a leaf like `IMAGE` — no new events, no children.

## Canonical vocabulary

`ICON_NAME` values are the *protocol contract*. The canonical names live in
`pathland_core::constants::icon` (`NAMES`, `is_canonical`) — the single
protocol-authoritative list every renderer and DSL binds to. An app may
reference a name the vocabulary does not (yet) contain; renderers fall back
however they own the mapping does, and the vocabulary can grow.

- **Navigation**: `home` `search` `menu` `close` `chevron-left` `chevron-right`
  `chevron-up` `chevron-down` `arrow-left` `arrow-right`
- **Actions**: `add` `remove` `check` `edit` `delete` `save` `share` `download`
  `upload` `refresh` `lock` `logout`
- **Media**: `play` `pause` `stop` `skip-back` `skip-forward` `volume`
  `volume-mute` `shuffle` `repeat` `music`
- **Status**: `info` `warning` `error` `success` `heart` `star` `bell` `cloud`
- **People**: `user` `users`
- **System**: `settings` `grid` `list` `filter`
- **Content**: `folder` `file` `image`

## Semantics

- **Authoring**: `Icon.make(i -> i.name(IconName.PLAY))` /
  `Icon.make(i -> i.name("play"))` (a canonical string, or an app-extension
  name), `Label.make(l -> l.title(title).icon(icon))`,
  `Button.make(b -> b.action(action)).children(Icon.make(i -> i.name(…)))`.
- **Size / tint**: `FONT_SIZE` / `COLOR` as on text. Sized like a symbol (the
  renderer owns its default size); tinted for the active scheme.
- **Reactivity**: the name is a single `Signal<String>` — a change re-emits only
  the node's `ICON_NAME` delta.
- **Accessibility**: `LABEL` makes the icon presentable; without one the icon is
  decorative (not announced, not interactive).

## Assessment

**Branch state:** `feat/qt-renderer` is 7 commits ahead of the merge base; `main` is **275 commits ahead**. The Qt renderer crates (`pathland-render-qt`, `pathland-render-core`) exist *only* on this branch — but `pathland-core` was modified on **both** sides, so the merge is a real conflict, not a fast-forward.

### What main changed that affects the Qt renderer

1. **Protocol rename (breaking):** `STYLE` category → `PARAMETER`, and the `style::` module → `parameter::`. Your `render-core/src/host.rs` and `renderer.rs` still reference `category::STYLE` / `style::SET_*`, so the merged core won't compile against them until renamed.
2. **New spec surface (on main, absent here):** `spec/MEDIA.md`, `spec/PROXY.md`, `spec/ICONS.md`, `spec/LAYOUT.md` — plus new components and events in the shared `constants.rs`.

### Spec-parity gap (Qt renderer vs. the merged protocol + GTK reference)

New components the Qt renderer must map (or treat as layout-transparent), mirroring GTK (`lib.rs` `widget_kind`):

| Component | Qt mapping needed |
|-----------|-------------------|
| `VIDEO` 0x0A | Media surface → `QtMultimedia` (new dep!) |
| `ICON` 0x0B | Icon → `ICON_NAME` → Qt-native glyph |
| `SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17 | Fit slot; measure width → report `FIT_CHANGED` |
| `GRID_ROW` 0x1D | Row grouping inside `GRID` |
| `PROXY_VIEW` 0x1E | Plain container (layout-transparent) |
| `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30 | **No widget** (non-visual, layout-transparent) |

New events/properties to handle: `MEDIA_*` event family, `FIT_CHANGED`, `FOCUS_CHANGED`/`EDITING_CHANGED`/`SUBMIT`/`SCROLL`/`WHEEL`/`DATE_CHANGED`, media transport props, `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`, `ICON_NAME`, `FIT_QUERY`, `GRID_COLUMNS/ROWS/TRACKS`, `OFFSET_*`, `MIN/IDEAL/MAX_WIDTH/HEIGHT`, etc.

Plus the **pre-existing gaps** already in `status.md`: pointer `hover`/`leave`, `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP`, `MENU` popup item list, native `DATE_PICKER`/`COLOR_PICKER`, `BACKGROUND_COLOR` on controls, `SHAPE` paths, lazy-view virtualization, `TRANSITION`, FILL inside `GRID`.

### Notable constraint

`build.rs` currently links `QtCore/QtGui/QtQml/QtQuick/QtQuickLayouts` only. `VIDEO` requires **QtMultimedia** (`brew install qtmultimedia`) — a new build/toolchain dependency and CI consideration.

---

## Proposed plan

**Phase 0 — Merge & make it build**
1. `git merge main` (or rebase — your call), resolve `pathland-core` conflicts (constants/conformance/events/lib/ring/tests).
2. Rename `STYLE`→`PARAMETER` / `style`→`parameter` in `render-core` + `render-qt`; update the shared decode for new commands (`SET_DATE` 0x04), components, and event ids.
3. Gate: `cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-render-core`, then `cargo build -p pathland-render-qt` (offscreen), and the wasm no_std guard.

**Phase 1 — Layout-transparent & container components (no new deps)**
`PROXY_VIEW` (plain container), `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (no widget, layout-transparent child handling), `GRID_ROW` (flatten rows), `ICON` (map `ICON_NAME` → Qt glyph), `SIZE_THAT_FITS` + `FIT_CHANGED` measurement.

**Phase 2 — Media (new QtMultimedia dep)**
`VIDEO` surface + `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` transport (`PLAYBACK_STATE`/`MEDIA_POSITION`/`MEDIA_VOLUME`/`MEDIA_RATE`/`MEDIA_MUTED`/`MEDIA_LOOP`) + `MEDIA_*` events; controller-keyed registry (mirror `sync_media`).

**Phase 3 — Remaining events & controls**
`FOCUS_CHANGED`/`EDITING_CHANGED`/`SUBMIT`/`SCROLL`/`WHEEL`/`DATE_CHANGED`, `hover`/`leave`, `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP`, `MENU` popup, native date/color pickers, `BACKGROUND_COLOR` on controls, `SHAPE` path, lazy virtualization, `TRANSITION`, FILL-in-GRID.

**Phase 4 — Verify & sync docs**
`cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (offscreen), full workspace `cargo test`, `mvn install` for the Java reactor, update `status.md`/`todo.md`.

## Finalized plan — merge `main` + full Qt renderer spec parity

### Phase 0 — Merge and re-platform the renderer
1. `git merge main` (or `git rebase main` if you prefer a linear history). Resolve `pathland-core` conflicts: `constants.rs`, `conformance.rs`, `events.rs`, `lib.rs`, `ring.rs`, and the tests.
2. **Rename** `STYLE`→`PARAMETER` / `style::`→`parameter::` across `pathland-render-core/src/{lib.rs,host.rs}` and `pathland-render-qt/src/renderer.rs` (+ any `run.rs`/`capi.rs` references).
3. **Update the shared decode** (`render-core/src/host.rs`) for the merged surface: `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` (0x04), new `component_type` ids, new `event::` ids, new `property_id` ids. Keep the decode component-agnostic and let the Qt layer decide mapping.
4. **Gate:** `cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-render-core`, `cargo build -p pathland-render-qt`, and the wasm no_std guard (`lib/rust/check-wasm.sh`).

### Phase 1 — Layout-transparent + container components (no new deps)
- `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30 → **no widget**, layout-transparent children (mirror GTK `lib.rs` "invisible" + `layout.rs` child handling).

## Short answer: no — keep the hybrid, don't rewrite in C++

First, a correction to the premise: the Qt integration is **already hybrid, and the part that is actually Qt is already C++**. The split is roughly even:

| Layer | Language | File(s) |
|-------|----------|---------|
| Qt/QML widget mapping, QML `Bridge` QObject | **C++** | `qt_layer.cpp` (1556 ln), `bridge.cpp` (84 ln) |
| Protocol decode, sent-state delta diff, token resolution, ring/C ABI | Rust | `render-core/host.rs`, `renderer.rs`, `ffi.rs`, `run.rs`, `capi.rs` |

So "Qt Quick's native language" is already where it needs to be — the actual scene-graph/widget work is C++. What's in Rust is **not Qt-specific at all**: it's the 16-byte opcode decode, design-token resolution, and diff logic.

### What a "pure C++ from scratch" rewrite actually means

You'd only be moving the **protocol layer** into C++, and you'd reimplement in C++:

- 16-byte opcode frame decode (TREE/PARAMETER/EVENT/META, arena strings, value-type packing)
- design-token resolution + color-scheme detection
- the sent-state delta diff ("unchanged tree emits zero opcodes")
- the entire event encoder (pointer/key/value/text + the new `MEDIA_*` family, echo suppression)
- ring/transport interop against `libpathland_core`
- golden-vector conformance tests

…and then maintain **two** decoders forever: Rust (GTK + HTML) and C++ (Qt), so every protocol change lands twice. That's the exact thing this branch just spent effort *eliminating*.

### The key fact you should know about this branch's direction

`pathland-render-core` (the shared Rust decode) **does not exist on `main`** — it was introduced on `feat/qt-renderer`, and the branch **also refactored GTK onto it** (`pathland-render-gtk/Cargo.toml` → `pathland-render-core`). So the whole thesis of this branch is "one tested, toolkit-free decode shared by every renderer." A C++ rewrite of Qt's decode directly contradicts that.

Note also: `main` advanced GTK's decode substantially (media/proxy/icons/fit). **Regardless of Qt's language choice**, `render-core` must absorb that work during the merge. That's the real cost, and it's independent of the Rust-vs-C++ question.

### What the actual pain point is (and it's not the language)

The real friction is the **Rust↔C++ FFI marshalling layer** (`PathlandQtCommand` batch + `PathlandQtEvent` in `ffi.rs`), not the language. If that seam bugs you, the fix is to *move where the boundary sits* — e.g. keep the decode in Rust and push the delta-diff down into C++ — rather than reimplement the protocol.

The one legitimate "more idiomatic C++" critique is that `qt_layer.cpp` builds QML items imperatively via `QObject::setProperty`, where QML prefers declarative construction (`QQmlComponent`-driven factories or generated QML). That's an improvement **inside the C++ layer**, orthogonal to Rust-vs-C++.

---

**Recommendation:** stay with the agreed hybrid plan (Rust shared decode + C++/QML widget layer). It keeps one conformance-tested decode, keeps ring/ABI interop in Rust where it already is, and the C++ layer already owns everything Qt-specific.

Want me to (a) proceed with the hybrid plan as agreed, or (b) write up a concrete pure-C++ alternative so you can compare the two costed out before deciding?
a

Confirmed — proceeding with the hybrid architecture (Rust shared decode + C++/QML widget layer), full spec parity, with QtMultimedia.

## Final plan

**Phase 0 — Merge & re-platform**
1. `git merge main`, resolve `pathland-core` conflicts (`constants.rs`, `conformance.rs`, `events.rs`, `lib.rs`, `ring.rs`, tests).
2. Absorb main's GTK decode advancements into `pathland-render-core` (media/proxy/icons/fit), since the branch already moved GTK onto it.
3. Rename `STYLE`→`PARAMETER` / `style::`→`parameter::` in `render-core` + `render-qt`.
4. Extend shared decode for `SET_DATE` (0x04) + new component/event/property ids.
5. **Gate:** `cargo test -p pathland-core -p pathland-render-core`, `cargo build -p pathland-render-qt` (offscreen), wasm no_std guard.

**Phase 1 — Layout-transparent + container components (no new deps)**
- `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` → no widget (layout-transparent); `PROXY_VIEW` → plain `Item`; `GRID_ROW` → row flattening; `ICON` → `ICON_NAME` → Qt glyph; `SIZE_THAT_FITS` + `FIT_CHANGED` measurement; new layout props (`OFFSET_*`, `POSITION_*`, `MIN/IDEAL/MAX_*`, `FIXED_SIZE_*`, `LAYOUT_PRIORITY`, `ASPECT_RATIO`, `CONTENT_MODE`, `GRID_COLUMNS/ROWS/TRACKS`).

**Phase 2 — Media (add QtMultimedia)**
- `build.rs` links QtMultimedia (+ `brew install qtmultimedia`, CI update).
- `VIDEO` → `MediaPlayer` + `VideoOutput`; controller-keyed registry; transport props + `MEDIA_*` events + echo suppression.

**Phase 3 — Remaining events & controls (close `status.md` gaps)**
- `FOCUS_CHANGED`/`EDITING_CHANGED`/`SUBMIT`/`SCROLL`/`WHEEL`/`DATE_CHANGED`, hover/leave, `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP`, BackSpace back, `MENU` popup, native date/color pickers, `BACKGROUND_COLOR` on controls, `SHAPE` paths, `PICKER` styling, lazy virtualization, `TRANSITION`, FILL-in-GRID.

**Phase 4 — Verify & sync docs**
- `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (offscreen), full workspace `cargo test`, `cd lib/java && mvn install`.
- Update `status.md` + `todo.md`; add per-phase regression tests.
```

# pathland-render-qt — todo / remaining work

Post-merge status (October 2026): `main` is merged into the branch and the
renderer maps the new protocol surface (icons, media, proxy views, fit slots,
grid rows). Remaining work is tracked here and in `status.md`.

## Done

- **`main` merged** (`PARAMETER` rename; the shared `pathland-render-core`
  absorbs the merged decode). Core/render-core/Qt tests green; wasm guard green.
- **New component mappings** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`):
  - `ICON` 0x0B → glyph `Text` from the canonical `ICON_NAME` map.
  - `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30 → non-visual (layout-transparent) `MediaPlayer` +
    `AudioOutput`.
  - `VIDEO` 0x0A → `VideoOutput`, bound via `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`.
  - `PROXY_VIEW` 0x1E → transparent vertical container.
  - `SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17 → greedy two-axis fill slot.
  - `GRID_ROW` 0x1D → `RowLayout` cell.
- **Media transport + reports** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`, `bridge.*`,
  `src/run.rs`): `MEDIA_SOURCE`, `PLAYBACK_STATE`, `MEDIA_POSITION`,
  `MEDIA_VOLUME`, `MEDIA_MUTED`, `MEDIA_LOOP`, `MEDIA_RATE`, and the
  `MEDIA_*` event family.
- **Layout/property parity**: offsets/positions, min/ideal/max sizes,
  content mode, clipping, border color/width/radius, text alignment/line
  limit/truncation, grid columns.
- **Headless test hang fixed**: the shell drops the executable directory from
  the QML import path at init, so `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` runs
  directly (~2s) instead of scanning `target/debug/deps` for minutes.
- **QtMultimedia** linked in `build.rs`; CI installs `qt6-multimedia-dev` +
  `qml6-module-qtmultimedia`.
- **Tests**: `new_components_and_media_binding`, `decode_maps_media_reports`;
  full crate 24/24 green.

## Still missing / needs doing

- [ ] **`SIZE_THAT_FITS` / `FIT_CHANGED`**: decode the `FIT_QUERY` `LIST`
      (arena `f32` thresholds) in `pathland-render-core` (or the Qt diff), then
      measure allocated width and report `FIT_CHANGED` so the app can switch
      candidates without a round trip.
- [ ] **`GRID_ROW` flattening**: attach a row's cells directly to the `Grid`
      (instead of one `RowLayout` cell) so columns align across rows.
- [ ] **Events**: pointer `hover`/`leave`, `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP`,
      `FOCUS_CHANGED`/`EDITING_CHANGED`/`SUBMIT`, BackSpace native back.
- [ ] **Asset root**: resolve `/_pathland/assets/...` to a local root for
      `MEDIA_SOURCE`/`IMAGE_SOURCE` (a `pathland_qt_set_asset_root` analogue of
      GTK's).
- [ ] **Controls gaps**: `MENU` popup item list, native `DATE_PICKER`/
      `COLOR_PICKER`, `PICKER` option styling, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`/border on
      Qt Quick Controls, `SHAPE` paths.
- [ ] **Lazy view virtualization** (currently eager) and `TRANSITION` animation.
- [ ] **Demo icons (cosmetic)**: the Qt demo references `icons/*.svg`; point it
      at real assets (or the shared `DemoAssets`) so sidebar rows show icons.

## Known constraints

- FILL inside a plain `QQuickGrid` is skipped (`Grid` rejects child anchors);
  stacks use `RowLayout`/`ColumnLayout` so FILL works there.
- Qt Quick Controls own their background delegate, so border/background on
  controls is limited.

1: //! # Pathland Qt Quick desktop demo
2: //!
3: //! A native Qt Quick app demonstrating Pathland's **zero-copy shared-memory
4: //! ring** and the shared **Qt renderer** (`pathland-render-qt`).
5: //!
6: //! The developer authors the UI with the SwiftUI-style DSL; the diff emitter
7: //! emits declarative 16-byte opcodes into the shared ring, and the Qt renderer
8: //! maps them onto a Qt Quick scene (Row/Column/Text/Button/TextField/Slider).
9: //! The demo never touches Qt APIs directly — it only drives Pathland and the
10: //! renderer.
11: //!
12: //! Interaction is declared with `.on_tap_gesture(...)` on any view; raw pointer
13: //! events round-trip through the shared ring and are turned back into taps by
14: //! the app-side [`TapRecognizer`](pathland_view::TapRecognizer).
15: 
16: use std::cell::RefCell;
17: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
18: use std::rc::Rc;
19: use std::time::Instant;
20: 
21: use pathland_engine::Engine;
22: use pathland_core::listener;
23: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;
24: use pathland_view::{
25:     assign_ids, button, hstack, text, vstack, Color, Node, Slider, View, ViewExt,
26: };
27: 
28: const APP_ID: &str = "org.pathland.QtDemo";
29: 
30: /// node id → tap callback, collected from the built tree after `assign_ids`.
31: type TapHandlers = BTreeMap<u32, Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>>;
32: 
33: /// Mark a node as a value-reporting control (`BINDING_ID`), so the renderer
34: /// gates its `VALUE_CHANGED` events back to the app. The Rust DSL does not yet
35: /// expose signal property bindings, so the demo marks the slider directly on
36: /// the retained tree (the protocol's "this node reports" marker).
37: fn mark_value_bound(node: &mut Node) {
38:     if node.component == pathland_view::Component::Slider {
39:         node.properties
40:             .insert(pathland_core::property_id::BINDING_ID, 1);
41:     }
42:     for child in &mut node.children {
43:         mark_value_bound(child);
44:     }
45: }
46: 
47: /// Build the DSL tree for the current counter + slider value. This is the
48: /// developer's authoring surface.
49: fn build_tree(count: &Rc<RefCell<u32>>, slider_value: &Rc<RefCell<f32>>) -> Node {
50:     let tap_count = count.clone();
51:     let mut tree = vstack![
52:         hstack![
53:             text(format!("Count: {}", *count.borrow()).as_str()),
54:             button("Increment").on_tap_gesture(move || *tap_count.borrow_mut() += 1),
55:         ]
56:         .spacing(8.0)
57:         .padding(16.0),
58:         text("Pathland · Qt Quick · shared ring").foreground_style(Color::argb(0xFF_888888)),
59:         // A non-button view (Text) declaring raw pointer listeners — proving any
60:         // element can emit events via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` property.
61:         text("I am a Text with raw pointer listeners")
62:             .pointer_events(listener::POINTER_DOWN | listener::POINTER_UP)
63:             .foreground_style(Color::argb(0xFF_0000AA)),
64:         text(format!("Slider: {:.1}", *slider_value.borrow()).as_str()),
65:         Slider {
66:             value: *slider_value.borrow(),
67:             min: 0.0,
68:             max: 10.0,
69:         },
70:         vstack![
71:             text("short"),
72:             text("a much longer label"),
73:             text("x"),
74:         ]
75:         .spacing(4.0)
76:         .padding(16.0),
77:     ]
78:     .spacing(12.0)
79:     .padding(24.0)
80:     .build();
81:     mark_value_bound(&mut tree);
82:     tree
83: }
84: 
85: fn main() {
86:     let engine = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Engine::new()));
87:     let ring = Rc::new(RefCell::new(RingTransport::new()));
88:     let count = Rc::new(RefCell::new(0u32));
89:     let slider_value = Rc::new(RefCell::new(5.0f32));
90:     let handlers = Rc::new(RefCell::new(TapHandlers::new()));
91: 
92:     // Build + emit the current tree, refreshing the id → tap-callback map.
93:     let emit = {
94:         let engine = engine.clone();
95:         let ring = ring.clone();
96:         let count = count.clone();
97:         let slider_value = slider_value.clone();
98:         let handlers = handlers.clone();
99:         move || {
100:             let mut tree = build_tree(&count, &slider_value);
101:             assign_ids(&mut tree, &mut 1);
102:             let mut h = handlers.borrow_mut();
103:             h.clear();
104:             pathland_view::collect_tap_handlers(&tree, &mut *h);
105:             drop(h);
106: 
107:             let mut ring_ref = ring.borrow_mut();
108:             let mut guest = ring_ref.producer();
109:             guest.begin_frame();
110:             engine.borrow_mut().emit(&tree, &mut guest).ok();
111:             guest.end_frame();
112:         }
113:     };
114: 
115:     // Initial frame before the renderer starts pumping.
116:     emit();
117: 
118:     // Hand the renderer the shared ring and a wake handler. The renderer writes
119:     // native inputs as EVENT opcodes into the ring and wakes us; we drain the
120:     // ring, run the taps through the recognizer, invoke the matching callback,
121:     // and re-emit. The renderer's idle pump applies the delta.
122:     pathland_qt::run(APP_ID, "Pathland Qt Demo", ring.clone(), {
123:         let emit = emit;
124:         let handlers = handlers.clone();
125:         let slider_value = slider_value.clone();
126:         let start = Instant::now();
127:         let mut recognizer = pathland_view::TapRecognizer::new();

132:             for ev in &events {

134:                 // request with no URL. There is no Rust router yet, so this is
135:                 // surfaced to the console to prove the event reached the app.
136:                 if matches!(ev, pathland_core::Event::Navigate { url: None }) {

141:                 // path applies it back without a loop.
142:                 if let pathland_core::Event::ValueChanged { value, .. } = ev {
143:                     *slider_value.borrow_mut() = *value;
144:                     changed = true;
145:                 }
146:                 if let Some(target) = recognizer.feed(ev, now_ms) {
147:                     if let Some(handler) = handlers.borrow().get(&target) {
148:                         let mut cb = handler.borrow_mut();
149:                         (&mut *cb)();
150:                         changed = true;
151:                     }
152:                 }
153:             }
154:             if changed {
155:                 emit();
156:             }
157:         }
158:     });
159: }

Done. `main` is fully merged into `feat/qt-renderer` and the renderer now covers the protocol surface that landed on `main`.

## What landed

**Merge (`47ae3bfa`)**
- Resolved 10 conflicts across `pathland-core`, `core-transport`, `render-core`, `render-gtk`, `view-native`, CI, and docs.
- Absorbed the `STYLE` → `PARAMETER` rename and the DSL API changes into `pathland-render-core`, the Qt crate, its tests, and the Rust Qt demo.
- `cargo check --workspace`, wasm no_std guard, and all core/render-core/Qt tests green.

**Component parity** (`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`)
- `ICON` → canonical-name → glyph map; `PROXY_VIEW` → transparent container; `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` → non-visual; `VIDEO` → `VideoOutput`; `SIZE_THAT_FITS` → greedy slot; `GRID_ROW` → row cell.
- Layout props: offsets/positions, min/ideal/max sizes, content mode, clipping, borders, text alignment/line-limit/truncation, grid columns.

**Media (`spec/MEDIA.md`)**
- QtMultimedia `MediaPlayer` + `AudioOutput`, `MEDIA_SOURCE`/`PLAYBACK_STATE`/`MEDIA_POSITION`/`MEDIA_VOLUME`/`MEDIA_MUTED`/`MEDIA_LOOP`/`MEDIA_RATE`, and the `MEDIA_*` event reports (`bridge.cpp`, `run.rs`).
- Asset-root resolution (`pathland_qt_set_asset_root`) mirroring GTK.

**Fixes**
- Root-caused the documented headless-test "hang": Qt scanned the huge `target/debug/deps` as an implicit QML import path. The shell now drops it — `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` runs directly (24/24 in ~2s).
- Migrated `lib/java/pathland-qt-demo` to `dev.pathland.demo.qt`, fixed the pom (`dev.pathland` parent/deps), mounted `SplitNavDemo` via `environmentBinding`, and wired `DemoAssets` — Maven reactor install + demo tests green.

## Remaining (documented in `status.md` / `todo.md`)
- `SIZE_THAT_FITS` `FIT_CHANGED` measurement (needs `FIT_QUERY` LIST decoding).
- `GRID_ROW` cross-row column alignment.
- Hover/leave, `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP`, focus/editing/submit, BackSpace back.
- `MENU` popup, native date/color pickers, `PICKER` styling, control backgrounds, `SHAPE` paths.
- Lazy-view virtualization and `TRANSITION` animation.

Branch is clean and 11 commits ahead of `main` (merge included).

content.text:
Good question — the "remains" aren't random leftovers; each has a specific reason. Here's the honest breakdown.

## Why each item remains

**Two are blocked on the shared decode core, not just Qt.**
- `SIZE_THAT_FITS` / `FIT_CHANGED`: `FIT_QUERY` is a `LIST`-typed value, but `pathland-render-core` (the crate the Qt renderer decodes through) stores `LIST` as a **raw arena offset** and never parses it. Only `pathland-render-html` decodes it (`list_f32` → `fit_thresholds`, `host.rs:1118`). GTK doesn't implement it either — there's no Rust reference, only Java/web. So it needs core changes + width measurement + a new event path.
- Native `DATE_PICKER` / `SET_DATE`: render-core also ignores the `parameter::SET_DATE` command (the HTML renderer handles it, core doesn't).

**The rest are Qt-native gaps, not merge/parity work:**
- `GRID_ROW` cross-row alignment — `QQuickGrid` has no row-grouping; requires flatten-into-grid bookkeeping (I shipped the "renders as a row" approximation).
- Hover/leave, `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP`, focus/editing/submit, BackSpace — each needs new event kinds + Qt signal wiring + focus tracking; mechanical but one-per-item.
- `MENU` popup and native date/color pickers — Qt Quick Controls has **no native** date/color picker and no `MenuButton`; they need custom QML popups/dialogs (a real design decision, not a TODO).
- Lazy virtualization and `TRANSITION` — larger rendering features.

## Final plan — complete the Qt renderer (A–E)

### A. Shared decode parity (`pathland-render-core/src/host.rs`)
- Add `lists: HashMap<u16, Vec<f32>>` and `date: Option<(i32, u32)>` to `HostNode`.
- Decode `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY` with `value_type::LIST` into `lists` (parse `[u32 count][f32 × count]` via `frame.arena_get`, mirroring `pathland-render-html`'s `list_f32`).
- Decode `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` (`op.b() as i32`, `op.c()`) into `date`.
- Tests: list-parse unit test + a hand-built `SET_DATE`/`LIST` frame.

### B. `SIZE_THAT_FITS` + `FIT_CHANGED`
- Qt diff serializes `lists[FIT_QUERY]` → CSV and emits it as the string property under `FIT_QUERY` (reuses `SET_STRING_PROPERTY`; no header change).
- C++ parses CSV thresholds; the fit-slot `Item` gets an `onWidthChanged` that derives the index (largest threshold ≤ width) and calls `bridge.fitChanged(id, index)` (only on change).
- New `PLQT_EV_FIT_CHANGED = 13`; `decode_event` → `Event::FitChanged { target, index }`.
- Test: threshold→index derivation (unit) + event decode.

### C. `GRID_ROW` flattening
- Track `grid_of: rowId → gridId`. On inserting a `GRID_ROW` into a `GRID`, re-parent its cells to the grid and skip the row item; on inserting a cell into a `GRID_ROW`, attach to its grid. Mirror on remove/delete.
- Test: grid with a `GRID_ROW` + a bare cell → correct flat child count.

### D. `DATE_PICKER` (QML approximation)
- New `PLQT_SET_DATE` command (`a=id, b=days(i32), c=millis(u32)`); C++ formats `QDate(1970,1,1).addDays(days)` + millis into the `TextField`'s text.
- Test: command applies a formatted date string.

### E. Raw-input events
- **Struct**: extend `PathlandQtEvent` with a trailing key payload (`uint16_t key_code; uint8_t modifiers; uint8_t repeat;`); existing constructors zero-init so no breakage.
- **Hover/leave**: `onEntered`/`onExited` on the listener MouseArea (gated by `POINTER_MOVE`) → `PLQT_EV_POINTER_ENTER/LEAVE` → `Event::PointerMove { hovering/leaving }`.
- **Keys**: extend `KeyFilter` to report `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` for the focused node with the key-listener bit; track `g.focused_id`. BackSpace → `Navigate` back when the focused node isn't a text editor.
- **Focus/editing/submit**: `TextField` `onActiveFocusChanged` / `onEditingFinished` → `PLQT_EV_FOCUS` / `PLQT_EV_EDITING` / `PLQT_EV_SUBMIT`, gated by the `FOCUS`/`EDITING`/`SUBMIT` listener bits.
- New `decode_event` mappings to `Event::{KeyDown,KeyUp,FocusChanged,EditingChanged,Submit}` + tests.

### Verify
- `cargo test -p pathland-render-core`, `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (offscreen), `cargo check --workspace`, wasm guard.
- Update `status.md`/`todo.md`.

I'll implement in this order (A → B → C → D → E), committing per phase. Ready when you are — approve to start.

content.text:
Done — phases A–E are implemented, green, and committed (`2b0535c4`).

## What closed

**A. Shared decode parity** (`pathland-render-core/src/host.rs`)
- `HostNode` now carries `lists` (`LIST`/`FIT_QUERY`) and `date` (`SET_DATE`), with `list_property()`.
- Decodes the arena `[u32 len][u32 count][f32 × count]` form the ring emitter writes.

**B. `SIZE_THAT_FITS` + `FIT_CHANGED`**
- The Qt diff forwards `FIT_QUERY` as CSV; the C++ slot parses it, derives the index from its allocated width on `widthChanged` (largest `minWidth` ≤ width), and reports `FIT_CHANGED` only on change.

**C. `GRID_ROW`**
- Row cells are flattened into the parent `Grid` (row-major, with a global index), so columns align across rows; the row item takes no cell.

**D. `DATE_PICKER`**
- New `PLQT_SET_DATE` command; the C++ layer formats days-since-epoch + millis into an ISO date (with time when nonzero) in a QML text field.

**E. Events**
- `PathlandQtEvent` gained a key payload; new kinds for enter/leave, key down/up, focus, editing, submit.
- Hover/leave via the listener `MouseArea`; keys reported for the focused text input (key-listener gated); focus/editing/submit gated by their `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits; BackSpace = native back unless a text input has focus.

## Verification
- `cargo test -p pathland-render-core`: 5/5; `-p pathland-render-qt`: **30/30** (offscreen).
- New tests: `decodes_list_and_date_values`, `list_property_is_forwarded_as_csv`, `size_that_fits_derives_index_from_width`, `grid_row_flattens_into_the_grid`, `date_change_is_forwarded_once`, `date_picker_formats_set_date`, `decode_maps_hover_key_and_focus`.
- `cargo check --workspace` and the wasm `no_std` guard pass.

## Still open (Phase F/G, as agreed)
`MENU` popup item list, `COLOR_PICKER` (QML popup), `PICKER` styling, control backgrounds/`SHAPE`, `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`/`DATE_CHANGED`, lazy virtualization, and `TRANSITION`. These are recorded in `status.md` / `todo.md`.
The qt demo does not render anything that looks remotely like the html or gtk demo

content.text:
## Diagnosis

The Qt demo renders the **structure** (stacks, text, buttons, controls) but almost none of the **chrome** — which is exactly what makes the HTML/GTK demos look the way they do. I traced the demo's modifier usage against what `qt_layer.cpp` actually applies:

| The demo uses | Qt renderer today |
|---|---|
| `background(...)` → `BACKGROUND_COLOR` 0x1001 | **not handled** (constant is defined, no `applyProperty` case) |
| `border(...)` + `cornerRadius(...)` | only on `Rectangle`-backed nodes (DIVIDER/COLOR/SHAPE), never on stacks/controls |
| `foregroundStyle(...)` → `COLOR` | applied to a bare `Text`; **lost** on composite `Label`/`Button` (the HStack wrapper has no `color`) |
| `Button` + `PlainButtonStyle`/`BorderedButtonStyle` (composite mode) | rendered as a **native** Qt `Button`; children attached via `setParentItem` (wrong layout), so sidebar rows look like default OS buttons with an overlay |
| cross-axis stretch (HTML `align-items:stretch` default) | not applied → sidebar/content collapse to content height instead of filling the window |
| `Spacer` | maps to an empty `Item` that doesn't expand |
| `shadow(...)` → `SHADOW_*` 0x1021-24 | not handled |

The two structural causes matter as much as the styling:
1. **Composite-control mode is missing.** In `Button.render`, the `ButtonStyle` body becomes the button's **child** (Composite Override Mode, PRIMITIVES.md §2) — the "chrome" is ordinary `background`/`border`/`padding`/`color` modifiers on that child. So a styled button is: a transparent clickable wrapper hosting a decorated child. The Qt renderer must render a `Button` *with children* as a bare container (no native chrome), not a `QQuickControl`.
2. **Default cross-axis stretch** (what the HTML flex `align-items:stretch` gives and the Sidebar comment explicitly relies on) is not applied, so the split view squishes vertically.

Icons also currently render as a small Unicode-glyph map (`home`→`⌂` etc.), so they differ from the SVG icons the web ships — secondary, but part of "looks like".

## Proposed plan — a visual-parity pass on `pathland-render-qt`

**S1. Background / border / radius layer.** For any node carrying `BACKGROUND_COLOR`/`BORDER_*`/`BORDER_RADIUS` (and transparent `Color.CLEAR`), attach a `Rectangle { anchors.fill; radius; border }` behind the content. Stacks already have a wrapper `Item` (reuse it); controls use their `background` delegate or the same approach.

**S2. Composite control mode.** `Button` (and other controls) **with children** render as a transparent `Item` + tap `MouseArea` hosting the child layout, with the existing `ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` tap reporting. Leaf controls keep the native widget.

**S3. Foreground color propagation.** When a container carries `COLOR`/`foregroundStyle`, apply it to descendant `Text`/`Icon` items (CSS `color` inheritance), so `Label`/`Button` text inherits the tint.

**S4. Layout defaults.** Default cross-axis stretch when `ALIGNMENT` is absent (match `align-items:stretch`); make `Spacer` expand on the main axis (`Layout.fillHeight`/`fillWidth`); `CONTENT_MARGINS`.

**S5. Shadow + text style + icon fidelity (secondary).** `SHADOW_*` → `RectangularGlow`; `TEXT_STYLE` → a font-size/weight table; swap glyph icons for `QIcon::fromTheme` (or an icon font) for a closer visual match.

**S6. Verify.** Add a headless render-to-image smoke (the `pathland_qt_layer_render_once` hook already exists) or screenshot of `SplitNavDemo`, plus a manual `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` eyeball.

Two decisions before I write this up as a commit sequence:

## Finalized plan — Qt renderer visual parity (S1–S6, native leaf buttons)

All work is in `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt` (C++ `src/qt/qt_layer.cpp` + `pathland_qt.h`/`bridge.*`, Rust `renderer.rs`/`ffi.rs` for any new commands), plus `status.md`/`todo.md`.

### S1. Background / border / radius layer
- Add a generic `ensureBackground(QQuickItem*)` that returns (or creates) a `Rectangle` child `pl<id>bg` with `anchors.fill: parent; z: -1`.
- `applyProperty` cases for `BACKGROUND_COLOR` (0x1001), `BORDER_WIDTH/COLOR` (0x1003/4), `BORDER_RADIUS` (0x1005): set `color`/`border.*`/`radius` on that rectangle (transparent `Color.CLEAR` → no fill).
- Stacks already have a wrapper `Item`; reuse it (inject the rectangle into the stack QML template). Non-visual (`MEDIA_CONTROLLER`) skips.
- `resetNode` resets these to defaults (transparent, no border, radius 0).

### S2. Composite control mode (spec Dual-Mode)
- Keep native `Button` for leaf buttons (your choice).
- On first `insertChild` into a `Button` (or other composite-capable control), **promote** it: swap the native widget for a bare `Item` + `MouseArea` tap shell (reusing the existing `promoteNavSlot` pattern), re-parent children, preserve tap→`ACTION_ID`/`BINDING_ID` reporting.
- This makes `PlainButtonStyle`/`BorderedButtonStyle` sidebar rows and the "Open kitchen sink" button render as their styled child content.

### S3. Foreground color propagation
- `COLOR` on a `Text`/`Icon` → its own `color`. On a **container** → store as `g.fg_colors[id]`; on insert, walk up ancestors and apply the inherited color to descendant `Text`/`Icon` that don't set their own (CSS `color` inheritance).

### S4. Layout defaults
- **Cross-axis stretch default**: for a stack child whose parent has no `ALIGNMENT`, apply the cross-axis `Layout.fill` (`fillHeight` in HStack, `fillWidth` in VStack) — matches HTML `align-items:stretch` and the Sidebar's comment.
- **Spacer**: `qmlFor(SPACER)` → expanding `Item`; in a stack layout set main-axis `Layout.fill`; no-op outside layouts.
- `CONTENT_MARGINS` (0x0005) → padding, if used.

### S5. Shadow + text style + icon fidelity
- `SHADOW_COLOR/RADIUS/X/Y` (0x1021-24) → a `RectangularGlow` (or `DropShadow`) layered under the item, like the background layer.
- `TEXT_STYLE` (0x1032) → a font-size/weight table over the `text_style` enum (`Headline`→bold 24, `Title2`→semibold 22, …).
- Icons: try `QIcon::fromTheme(ICON_NAME)`, fall back to the existing glyph map (theme icons are spotty on macOS/offscreen, so this is best-effort; the glyphs stay as the safe path).

### S6. Verify
- New headless tests via the existing hook pattern: background/border/radius applied on the background rectangle; button promotes to composite and renders a child; inherited foreground color reaches a `Label`'s `Text`; spacer fills the main axis; default cross-axis stretch.
- `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (offscreen), `cargo check --workspace`, wasm guard.
- Manual `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` eyeball.
- Update `status.md`/`todo.md` (styling layer now implemented; remaining gaps shrink to lazy virtualization, `TRANSITION`, `MENU` popup, native date/color).

I'll implement in this order (S1 → S2 → S3 → S4 → S5 → S6), committing per step. Say the word when you want me to start.

- `SIZE_THAT_FITS` (0x17) → a greedy two-axis slot; its one selected child
    fills it.
  - `GRID_ROW` (0x1D) → a `RowLayout` cell (renders; cross-row column
    alignment is still a gap).
- **Shared decode parity** (`pathland-render-core`): `LIST`-typed properties
  (`FIT_QUERY`) decode into `HostNode::lists`, and `PARAMETER::SET_DATE` into
  `HostNode::date` — so the Qt layer can measure fit slots and format dates.
- **`SIZE_THAT_FITS` fit measurement**: the slot's `FIT_QUERY` thresholds reach
  the C++ layer as CSV; a width change derives the fit index (largest
  `minWidth` ≤ allocated width) and reports `FIT_CHANGED` (only when it
  changes).
- **`GRID_ROW` flattening**: a row's cells attach directly to the parent Grid
  (row-major), so columns align across rows; the row item takes no cell.
- **`DATE_PICKER`**: `SET_DATE` (days since epoch + millis of day) renders as an
  ISO date (with time when nonzero) in a QML text field — a QML approximation
  (Qt Quick has no native date picker).
- **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md): pointer `hover`/`leave` (`POINTER_MOVE`
  hovering/leaving) from the listener `MouseArea`; `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` for the
  focused text input (component-type/key-listener gated); `FOCUS_CHANGED` /
  `EDITING_CHANGED` / `SUBMIT` for text inputs (gated by the matching
  `EVENT_LISTENERS` bits); BackSpace is native back unless a text input is
  focused (focus-aware, no longer deferred).
- **Media transport** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_SOURCE`, `PLAYBACK_STATE`
  (play/pause), `MEDIA_POSITION` (seek, seconds→ms), `MEDIA_VOLUME` /
  `MEDIA_MUTED` (via `AudioOutput`), `MEDIA_LOOP`, `MEDIA_RATE`, and the
  `MEDIA_PLAY_STATE_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_TIME_UPDATED` / `MEDIA_ENDED` /
  `MEDIA_VOLUME_CHANGED` / `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` reports (reported by the
  controller's component type, not gated by `BINDING_ID`; programmatic sets are
  echo-suppressed). A play/pause declared before the source is re-applied when
  the source lands.
- **Layout/property parity**: `OFFSET_X/Y`, `POSITION_X/Y`, `MIN/IDEAL/MAX_*`,
  `CONTENT_MODE` (image fit/fill), `CLIPS_TO_BOUNDS`, `BORDER_COLOR` /
  `BORDER_WIDTH` / `BORDER_RADIUS`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `LINE_LIMIT`,
  `TRUNCATION_MODE`, and `GRID_COLUMNS` (via the `Layout` attached properties
  where applicable).
- **Headless test hang fixed**: Qt adds the executable's directory to QML's
  implicit import path; a `cargo test` binary lives in a huge `target/debug/deps`
  and plugin resolution scanned it for minutes. The shell now drops the
  application directory from the engine's import path at init, so
  `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` completes in ~2s (no copy-to-temp workaround).

## Not implemented / gaps

- **`MENU` popup item list**: Qt 6 has no `MenuButton`; the trigger is a
  `Button` and the action-item popup is not built (documented gap).
- **`COLOR_PICKER`** remains a `Button` approximation (a QML color-swatch popup
  is a follow-up); `DATE_PICKER` is an ISO-text QML approximation, not a native
  dialog.
- **`PICKER` option styling**, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`/border on Qt Quick Controls
  (they own their background delegate; border mapping covers `Rectangle`-backed
  nodes only), and `SHAPE` path approximation.
- **Keys/events beyond the focused text input**: keys are reported for a focused
  text input; keys on other focused controls, `SCROLL`/`WHEEL`, and
  `DATE_CHANGED` are not yet reported. Hover/leave use `POINTER_MOVE` (the
  listener mask bit).
- **FILL inside plain positioners**: `GRID` (a `QQuickGrid`) rejects
  `anchors.fill` on its children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a Grid
  defers and is skipped (the positioner sizes it). Stacks use `RowLayout`/
  `ColumnLayout` so FILL children stretch properly.
- The Rust DSL does not yet expose signal property bindings (the Java DSL
  does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
  tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.
- The Rust DSL has no `NavigationContainer` (the spec table is aspirational) —
  the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH; Java/SplitNavDemo is the nav demo
  vehicle.
- `TRANSITION`-hint animation, back-swipe gestures, multi-step deep-link
  intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).
- **Java JNA demo** (`lib/java/pathland-qt-demo`) runs the shared
  `SplitNavDemo` (incl. native navigation) via `pathland_qt_run_ring`.
- Lazy views render eagerly.

# pathland-render-qt — todo / remaining work

Post-merge status (October 2026): `main` is merged into the branch and the
renderer maps the new protocol surface (icons, media, proxy views, fit slots,
grid rows). Remaining work is tracked here and in `status.md`.

## Done

- **`main` merged** (`PARAMETER` rename; the shared `pathland-render-core`
  absorbs the merged decode). Core/render-core/Qt tests green; wasm guard green.
- **New component mappings** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`):
  - `ICON` 0x0B → glyph `Text` from the canonical `ICON_NAME` map.
  - `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` 0x30 → non-visual (layout-transparent) `MediaPlayer` +
    `AudioOutput`.
  - `VIDEO` 0x0A → `VideoOutput`, bound via `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID`.
  - `PROXY_VIEW` 0x1E → transparent vertical container.
  - `SIZE_THAT_FITS` 0x17 → greedy two-axis fill slot.
  - `GRID_ROW` 0x1D → `RowLayout` cell.
- **Media transport + reports** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`, `bridge.*`,
  `src/run.rs`): `MEDIA_SOURCE`, `PLAYBACK_STATE`, `MEDIA_POSITION`,
  `MEDIA_VOLUME`, `MEDIA_MUTED`, `MEDIA_LOOP`, `MEDIA_RATE`, and the
  `MEDIA_*` event family.
- **Layout/property parity**: offsets/positions, min/ideal/max sizes,
  content mode, clipping, border color/width/radius, text alignment/line
  limit/truncation, grid columns.
- **Asset root** (`pathland_qt_set_asset_root`): `/_pathland/...` sources
  resolve against a host-extracted local directory.
- **Java Qt demo migrated** to `dev.pathland.demo.qt` (view/demo package
  renames, `environmentBinding` mount, `DemoAssets` extraction).
- **Headless test hang fixed**: the shell drops the executable directory from
  the QML import path at init, so `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` runs
  directly (~2s) instead of scanning `target/debug/deps` for minutes.
- **QtMultimedia** linked in `build.rs`; CI installs `qt6-multimedia-dev` +
  `qml6-module-qtmultimedia`.
- **Tests**: `new_components_and_media_binding`, `decode_maps_media_reports`;
  full crate 24/24 green.

## Still missing / needs doing

- [x] **`SIZE_THAT_FITS` / `FIT_CHANGED`** — shared `LIST` decode + width measure
      + `FIT_CHANGED`.
- [x] **`GRID_ROW` flattening** — cells attach to the Grid; columns align.
- [x] **Events** — hover/leave, keys (focused text input),
      focus/editing/submit, BackSpace native back.
- [x] **`DATE_PICKER`** — `SET_DATE` → ISO text (QML approximation).
- [ ] **Controls gaps**: `MENU` popup item list, `COLOR_PICKER` (QML popup),
      `PICKER` option styling, `BACKGROUND_COLOR`/border on Qt Quick Controls,
      `SHAPE` paths. (`DATE_PICKER` is an ISO-text approximation.)
- [ ] **Lazy view virtualization** (currently eager) and `TRANSITION` animation.
- [ ] **Demo icons (cosmetic)**: the Qt demo references `icons/*.svg`; point it
      at real assets (or the shared `DemoAssets`) so sidebar rows show icons.

## Known constraints

- FILL inside a plain `QQuickGrid` is skipped (`Grid` rejects child anchors);
  stacks use `RowLayout`/`ColumnLayout` so FILL works there.
- Qt Quick Controls own their background delegate, so border/background on
  controls is limited.

content.text:
Implemented the visual-parity pass (S1–S6) and committed it (`ee97c82e`, `6abc7e43`, plus the log cleanup).

## What was wrong

The Qt renderer rendered the demo's **structure** but dropped its **chrome**. Concretely, `BACKGROUND_COLOR` was never applied (constant defined, no handler), borders/radii only worked on `Rectangle` nodes, foreground colors were lost on composite `Label`/`Button`, buttons rendered as native OS widgets instead of their `ButtonStyle` child content, and stacks didn't stretch cross-axis — so the split view collapsed and looked nothing like the HTML/GTK demo.

## What landed

- **S1 — background/border/radius**: a background `Rectangle` behind container content (injected `pl<id>bg` for stacks, created lazily for plain containers); `BACKGROUND_COLOR`/`BORDER_*`/`BORDER_RADIUS` set it; `RESET_NODE` clears it.
- **S2 — composite control mode**: a `Button` that gains children is promoted from the native widget to a bare `Item`+`ColumnLayout` shell that renders its `ButtonStyle` body (sidebar rows, "Open kitchen sink"). Leaf buttons stay native per spec.
- **S3 — foreground inheritance**: a container's `COLOR` propagates to descendant `Text`/`Icon` (CSS `color`), with own colors winning.
- **S4 — layout defaults**: cross-axis stretch when `ALIGNMENT` is absent (matches `align-items:stretch`), `Spacer` expands on the main axis, `CONTENT_MARGINS`.
- **S5 — typography/shadow**: `TEXT_STYLE` applies base size+weight (raw font props override, ordering handled in the diff); `SHADOW_*` renders a best-effort offset layer.
- **Extra**: `Text` now word-wraps within its allocated width (so long descriptions don't overflow like a single line).

## Verification

- Qt crate **35/35** tests pass (offscreen), including the new `container_background_border_and_radius`, `button_with_child_renders_composite`, `foreground_color_inherits_to_text`, `default_stack_stretch_and_spacer`, `text_style_and_shadow`.
- `cargo check --workspace` and the wasm `no_std` guard pass.
- The **Java Qt demo runs headlessly for 20 s without crashing** with the rebuilt dylib (the old `hs_err` logs in the tree are from an earlier run; I removed the tracked one and git-ignored crash logs).
- `mvn -pl pathland-qt-demo test` passes.

Run `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` to eyeball it — the sidebar background/border, flat styled menu rows, title typography, wrapping text, and full-height split should now resemble the web/GTK demos. Remaining fidelity gaps (icons are glyphs not SVG, shadows are an offset rectangle, `MENU` popup/`COLOR_PICKER`/`SHAPE`, lazy/transitions) are recorded in `status.md`/`todo.md`.
